audits.title: 1565 In Covid-19 Pandemic, Following the Updated Royal College of Surgeons of England Guidelines in Management of Acute Appendicitis; A General District Hospital Audit
audits.standard: Updated RCS England COVID-19 guidance: conservative treatment of acute appendicitis unless unresponsive or complicated
audits.setting: Kettering General Hospital, district general hospital

cycle1.result: Conservative treatment in 16/63 (25.4%), successful in 10/16 (63%); operative management first in 47/63 (74.6%).

audits.other_findings: Readmissions 3/16 (18.75%) after conservative vs 1/47 (2.12%) after operative management; no complications after failed conservative treatment. Re-audit planned.
audits.citation: Dorra A, Abdellatif M, Fahmy W, Salama Y. 1565 In Covid-19 Pandemic, Following the Updated Royal College of Surgeons of England Guidelines in Management of Acute Appendicitis; A General District Hospital Audit. British Journal of Surgery. 2021;108(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znab259.176.

audits.title: TU8.7 An audit of the investigation and management of acute appendicitis at a tertiary referral centre in Ireland
audits.standard: World Society of Emergency Surgery (WSES) Jerusalem guidelines 2020 for investigation, diagnosis and management of acute appendicitis
audits.setting: University Hospital Limerick, tertiary referral centre

cycle1.result: Clinical scores documented in 2.6% (n=1); CT 33.3% (n=13), ultrasound 33.3% (n=13), no imaging 33.3% (n=13); 100% managed surgically; average time to theatre 16.9 hours; 100% had histopathology; negative appendicectomy 15.4% (n=6).

audits.other_findings: Compliant for timely surgery and routine histopathology; 74.4% laparoscopic, 23.1% open; average length of stay 3.6 days. An educational intervention on clinical scoring systems was proposed.
audits.citation: Alanza U, Julius B, Merrigan A, Baban C, Tormey S. TU8.7 An audit of the investigation and management of acute appendicitis at a tertiary referral centre in Ireland. British Journal of Surgery. 2022;109(Supplement_5). doi:10.1093/bjs/znac248.080.

audits.title: MTP8.11 A Service Review and Retrospective Audit of Diagnostic Imaging and Clinical Outcomes in Acute Appendicitis: Evaluating Service and Adherence to the World Society of Emergency Surgery 2020 Guidelines
audits.standard: World Society of Emergency Surgery 2020 guidelines for acute appendicitis
audits.setting: Leighton Hospital, Mid Cheshire Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Pre-operative imaging in 92.5%; CT PPV 96.9%; CT used in 96% of patients over 40; 89.1% had appendicectomy within 24 hours; negative appendicectomy rate 4.2%; postoperative complications 10.1%.

audits.other_findings: 45.2% discrepancy between CT and intra-operative grading of complicated versus uncomplicated appendicitis; drain use 34.4%; mean LOS 8.5 days for complicated cases.
audits.citation: Iqbal Z, Abdalla O, Hussain A. MTP8.11 A Service Review and Retrospective Audit of Diagnostic Imaging and Clinical Outcomes in Acute Appendicitis: Evaluating Service and Adherence to the World Society of Emergency Surgery 2020 Guidelines. British Journal of Surgery. 2025;112(Supplement_13). doi:10.1093/bjs/znaf166.217.

audits.title: TPT 3.11 Evaluating Emergency Appendicectomy Practice in a District General Hospital: A Retrospective Audit
audits.standard: National guidance on timely surgery, preoperative imaging and postoperative antibiotic prescribing for emergency appendicectomy
audits.setting: District general hospital, Dudley Group NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Surgery within 24 hours of decision in 73.4%; 45.0% of delays justified, 41.0% due to theatre capacity; preoperative imaging 61.3%; acute pathology on histology 79.0%; postoperative antibiotics 67.2%.

audits.other_findings: 27.3% of CT-diagnosed and 25.0% of ultrasound-diagnosed appendicitis were histologically negative; antibiotic choice and duration varied widely. Re-audit planned.
audits.citation: Holmes C, Yantin R, Sellahewa S, Mahappuge S. TPT 3.11 Evaluating Emergency Appendicectomy Practice in a District General Hospital: A Retrospective Audit. British Journal of Surgery. 2026;113(Supplement_8). doi:10.1093/bjs/znag087.194.

audits.title: TPW 5.08 Improving Outcomes in Emergency Laparoscopic Appendicectomy: A Two-Cycle Audit in a UK Tertiary Centre
audits.standard: National and WSES recommendations for laparoscopic appendicectomy
audits.setting: Royal Sussex County Hospital, tertiary centre

cycle1.result: Time to diagnosis 16.8 hours; diagnosis to surgery 28.1 hours; CT 80%; scoring system use 0%; negative appendicectomy 8.9%; drains 44%; postoperative antibiotics 92.1%; complications 17.8%.

cycle2.result: Time to diagnosis 8.27 hours; diagnosis to surgery 20.54 hours; CT 77.8%; scoring system use 3.3%; negative appendicectomy 7.7%; drains 31%; postoperative antibiotics 75.6%; complications 3.3%.

audits.other_findings: Scoring system use remained low; cycle 2 complications were exclusively postoperative ileus.
audits.citation: Mohamed M, Selorfia S, Ahmed M. TPW 5.08 Improving Outcomes in Emergency Laparoscopic Appendicectomy: A Two-Cycle Audit in a UK Tertiary Centre. British Journal of Surgery. 2026;113(Supplement_8). doi:10.1093/bjs/znag087.350.
